chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-'Abbas, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abd Allah, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a woman who performs ghusl (ritual bath) from janabah, then afterward sees the man's semen. Is ghusl required upon her? He said, "No."

Then al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: It is appropriate for the junub not to put his hand into the vessel until he has washed it three times. What indicates this has already passed in the chapter on the rulings of taharah (ritual purity).

Then he said: He should mention Allah the Exalted by name at the time of his ghusl, glorify Him, and declare His transcendence. Then when he has finished his ghusl, let him say: O Allah, purify my heart.

key_terms.الطَّهَارَةِ: ritual purity and its legal rulings
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in the state of janabah
key_terms.طَهِّرْ قَلْبِي: purify my heart; a supplication after ghusl
key_terms.غُسْلٌ: the ritual bath required for major impurity

ai.seo_question: Does a woman need to repeat ghusl if she sees the man's semen after bathing from janabah?
ai.summary: This hadith states that if a woman performs ghusl from janabah and then later sees the man's semen, no further ghusl is required upon her. It also mentions recommended etiquette for the junub: washing the hand before putting it into a vessel, remembering Allah during ghusl, and reciting a brief du'a afterward.
